newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary '96 budget on IMF-agreed target - ministry.
newsitem.headline: Hungary '96 budget on IMF-agreed target - ministry.

text.p: Hungary's 1996 central budget deficit will be probably lower than planned, and the savings are likely to cover the wider-than-expected gap of the social security budget, the Finance Ministry said on Thursday.
"The central budget is likely to close the year with a deficit of 150 to 170 billion forints," Secretary of State Csaba Laszlo told a news conference.

He said this was likely to help Hungary keep the deficit of the overall state budget below four percent of gross domestic product (GDP), which Hungary undertook in a stand-by loan agreement with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) in March.
The wider state budget includes the central state budget, the social security, state funds and the local munipalities.
The central budget deficit increased by some 36 billion forints to an accumulated 111 billion in November and was likely to rise some 75 to 90 billion forints in December, Laszlo added.
The central state budget's final position will be improved by one-off revenues of 34 billion forints, he added.
Hungary's central budget deficit target for this year, not including privatisation revenues, is 233 billion forints.
Local municipalities are seen ending the year with a surplus of 15 to 20 billion forints, but the state funds are likely to post a deficit of five to 10 billion forints.

The gap in the social security budget was already 67.3 billion forints in October, compared with the original 1996 target of 17.8 billion, and the total 1996 deficit is likely to exceed the 61 billion forecast in the supplementary budget of the social security, Laszlo said.
He added that Hungary planned to reduce the social security deficit to 13.5 billion forints next year.
The Finance Ministry originally planned a break-even social security deficit for 1997, but subsequent modifications softened the budget.
"This is a small change," Laszlo said.
Hungary's GDP will be around 6,600 billion forints in 1996.
